mobile_ap.executive_summary: Mobile AP competitive surface is fragmenting along AI inference architecture and manufacturing partnership lines. Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro operationalizes LogicFolding silicon-level optimization, Samsung courts both Snapdragon and in-house Exynos 2700 for S27 variants while partnering with Mistral AI on semiconductor engineering, and Qualcomm deepens data-center AI positioning through AWS collaboration—signaling a shift where mobile AI performance now trades against ecosystem lock-in and regional supply chain resilience rather than pure GPU-core density.

custom_soc.executive_summary: Nvidia's 85% market grip persists as infrastructure moat, but the competitive surface is fragmenting at the interposer layer—Qualcomm's multi-generational Amazon deal and Google's claimed 50% TPU inference cost advantage signal hyperscalers are now willing to co-engineer silicon boundaries rather than merely accept Nvidia's reference designs. Broadcom, Realtek (3nm ASIC orders secured), and emerging players like HyperAccel/SEMIFIVE are capturing peripheral AI workloads (inference, transmission), but none yet threaten Nvidia's core training-to-inference stack integration or its installed-base lock-in at the hardware-software boundary.

cpo_optics.executive_summary: CPO production timelines and funding intensity sharply accelerate: Ayar Labs secured $650M in 2026 funding for manufacturing scale, TSMC leads a 30-firm silicon photonics alliance addressing AI power crisis, and MIT breakthroughs on wafer-scale photonics flexibility hint at lower-cost integration paths. The competitive frontier has shifted from packaging feasibility to capital availability and supply-chain orchestration; players without heavy venture/foundry backing (Ayar, Crealights) now race against established optical vendors (Coherent, VIAVI, Keysight) who leverage testing and measurement infrastructure to capture the integration boundary.

hbm.executive_summary: HBM supply concentration intensifies as Samsung redirects half its 4nm capacity to HBM4 production while SK hynix transitions to 1c DRAM process by 1Q27, effectively narrowing the qualified vendor base. AMD's supply constraint acknowledgment and price escalation across Chinese AI chipmakers (Huawei 950DT up 50%) signal tightening availability beyond 2026. Synaptics' EDA integration with Ansys targets chip-to-system design parity, but remains marginal to the core capacity constraint dominating competitive positioning.

pmic.executive_summary: SMIC's 40.6 billion yuan internal restructuring (SMIC North buyout) clears regulatory hurdles, consolidating 8-inch mature-node capacity under single entity to optimize fab utilization and cost structure amid AI-driven capacity crowdout. This consolidation signals SMIC's strategic pivot to lock supply leverage in commodity BCD segments, but regulatory friction from US export restrictions remains a structural cost headwind that could limit margin sustainability.
